## 1. Audit commands and reproducibility

```bash
pnpm audit --json > full.json   # exit 1 (advisories present), stderr empty, valid JSON
pnpm audit --prod --json > prod.json
pnpm audit --dev --json > dev.json
```

Exit code 1 means "vulnerabilities found", not a registry/network failure: all outputs parsed as JSON, `advisories` objects were populated, stderr was empty, and `muted` was `[]` (nothing hidden by audit config). No `.npmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `auditConfig`, or `ignore*` settings exist in the repo; no overrides were added; no suppression or audit-level filtering is configured. `--prod` classifies dependencies; it does not prove runtime exploitability. `--dev` findings are build/CI supply-chain exposure only.

Review re-run (2026-11-12, at `fed3d1e`, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`): exits `full=1 prod=1 dev=1`, stderr empty, `muted: []`, all three outputs valid JSON with populated `advisories` and `metadata`. Results reconcile exactly with the post-remediation investigation (§2) — see §4 for the re-run table.

## 4. Production advisory ledger (current, verified at `fed3d1e`)

All four remaining production findings are one root cause: **Next.js 15.5.29 pins `postcss: 8.4.31` exactly** (verified in `node_modules/next/package.json`; `nuqs@2.9.4` peers on the same Next instance). `next@15.5.29` is the latest stable 15.5.x (15.6.x line is canary-only; Next 16 upgrade is out of scope/prohibited). No compatible in-range fix exists; an override would be an unverified change to Next's internal CSS pipeline and is recorded as an owner decision instead.

### 4.0 What was directly verified in the application (2026-11-12, source inspection)

- The only CSS source files in the repo are `app/globals.css` (and framework-injected Tailwind output). No `*.module.css`, no user-uploaded or CMS-themed CSS, no API route or Server Action accepts CSS text (`app/api/**` handles workspaces/issues/GitHub/search only; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in `app/` or `components/`).
- No file in the repository contains a `sourceMappingURL` comment (tree-wide grep, excluding `node_modules`).
- `postcss.config.mjs` registers only `@tailwindcss/postcss`; `next.config.ts` has no `postcss` or source-map settings; Next is invoked via `next build` / `next dev --turbopack` — note: Turbopack's CSS pipeline may not use PostCSS at all for app CSS, and in either case it does not process attacker-supplied CSS in this app (assumption, not independently instrumented).
- Next's PostCSS invocation context (`from` set? `map` option?) is **not directly observable from the repo** — recorded as an unverified assumption in §4.6. The advisory prerequisites below are stated from the primary advisories, not inferred from Next internals.
- PostCSS executes at build time in this project; no request-time code path in `app/` or `components/` calls PostCSS.

### 4.1 GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q — high (CVE-2026-45623, CVSS 7.5, EPSS 0.608%)

Prerequisite (primary advisory, published 2026-07-20, updated 2026-07-23): an attacker controls a CSS string passed to `postcss().process()`; PostCSS's `PreviousMap` parses `/*# sourceMappingURL=PATH */` and dereferences `PATH` on the local filesystem with no scheme/allowlist/traversal check — with **default options** (only `map:false` short-circuits). Non-JSON targets yield the first ~10 bytes of the file via the `JSON.parse` SyntaxError message; also a file-existence oracle and a DoS primitive (`/dev/zero`, large files).

EGA Work assessment:

- Directly verified: no repo source calls PostCSS at request time; no user-controlled CSS enters the build; the only processed stylesheet (`app/globals.css`) is authored in-tree and contains no `sourceMappingURL`.
- Conditions that would make this exploitable here: (a) a future feature accepts and builds user/third-party CSS (theme upload, CMS, email/invoice rendering), or (b) CI/build processes third-party CSS tarballs/checkouts whose content is attacker-influenced, or (c) a dependency upgrade begins running PostCSS on generated/derived CSS from external sources.
- Not identified in this app: any endpoint, build step, or dependency path that processes untrusted CSS text; any surfacing of PostCSS error messages to end users.
- Unverified assumptions: whether Next 15.5.29's build passes `from` and/or `map` when processing app CSS; Turbopack vs PostCSS pipeline split under `--turbopack` (dev only; `next build` uses webpack). Even under a silent default, the input is still in-tree CSS.
- Invalidating changes: any of (a)–(c) above, or removal of the no-untrusted-CSS invariant.

Confidence: low demonstrated exposure under documented assumptions. Advisory remains unresolved (no compatible patch in Next 15.5.x).

### 4.2 GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 — high (CVE-2026-73646, CVSS 7.5, EPSS 0.53%)

Prerequisite (primary advisory, published 2026-07-20, updated 2026-08-13): attacker-controlled `sourceMappingURL` in parsed CSS triggers auto-loading of the target as a _previous source map_; the `.map`-extension check added in 8.5.12 does not constrain traversal (`join(dirname(from), annotation)` allows `../` escape; absolute path verbatim when `from` is unset). The loaded map's `sourcesContent` is folded into `result.map` even if the caller never set `map`. Exploitation requires untrusted CSS **and** a consumer that exposes/uses `result.map` (playground/minify services, build pipelines emitting maps next to output).

EGA Work assessment:

- Directly verified: same input inventory as 4.1 — no untrusted CSS, no `.map` consumer in app code, no source maps published from user-derived CSS.
- Conditions that would make this exploitable here: the app (or its build) processes untrusted CSS **and** emits/serves the resulting `.map` (or surfaces `result.map`); or a third-party package processed at build time ships a malicious `sourceMappingURL` and the build infra auto-loads it.
- Not identified: any path returning `result.map` to clients; any `.map` file being served that was generated from third-party CSS.
- Unverified assumptions: whether `next build` sets `from` when running PostCSS (likely yes for file-based CSS, but not verified); whether Vercel's build exposes `result.map` artifacts beyond the deployment bundle.
- Invalidating changes: (a)–(c) from 4.1, or publishing source maps derived from third-party content.

Confidence: low demonstrated exposure under documented assumptions (`.map`-only targets, JSON-parseable maps only). Advisory remains unresolved.

### 4.3 GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp — moderate (CVE-2026-69153, CVSS v4 6.3, EPSS 0.451%)

Prerequisite (primary advisory, published 2026-07-24, updated 2026-08-03): incomplete fix of GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q. The `..`/absolute-path rejection is nested inside `if (cssFile)`; when PostCSS is invoked **without** `from`, only the `.map`-extension check remains, so an absolute `.map` path (or `../` traversal) in the CSS comment is read verbatim, and its `sources`/`sourcesContent` are disclosed via the generated map. Requires untrusted CSS processed without `from` **and** consumption of `result.map`.

EGA Work assessment:

- Directly verified: same input inventory; no code path processes CSS without a file context that could carry attacker input; no `result.map` consumer.
- Conditions that would make this exploitable here: identical class of exposure as 4.2, specifically via a PostCSS call made without `from` on untrusted CSS (e.g., a future stringify/minify playground).
- Not identified: such a call. Not identified: any serving of `.map` generated from untrusted input.
- Unverified assumptions: Next's `from` behavior (as above) — this specific advisory is _worsened_ if Next ever invokes PostCSS without `from`, but the impact still requires untrusted CSS input, which does not exist in this app today (documented assumption).
- Invalidating changes: same as 4.2; plus any introduction of string-input PostCSS invocations (online CSS tooling, email rendering, test fixtures fed from external sources).

Confidence: low demonstrated exposure under documented assumptions. Advisory remains unresolved.

### 4.4 GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 — moderate (CVE-2026-41305, CVSS 6.1, EPSS 0.205%)

Prerequisite (primary advisory, published 2026-04-20, updated 2026-04-24): user-submitted CSS is parsed and re-stringified for embedding in an HTML `<style>` tag; unescaped `</style>` in CSS values breaks out of the style context → XSS. Per the advisory itself: impacts _non-bundler_ use cases; requires the page to embed the stringified CSS inline.

EGA Work assessment:

- Directly verified: no `<style>{userCss}</style>` embedding anywhere; no CSS-in-HTML injection sink (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` absent); all served CSS is static, build-generated from in-repo sources.
- Conditions that would make this exploitable here: a future feature renders user/third-party CSS inline in HTML, or an error/debug page reflects PostCSS-stringified CSS into HTML.
- Not identified: any such reflection or embedding path.
- Unverified assumptions: none specific beyond the absence of the embedding pattern (verified by grep).
- Invalidating changes: any inline embedding of stringified third-party CSS, or a debug/error page that echoes processed CSS into HTML without escaping.

Confidence: low demonstrated exposure under documented assumptions. Advisory remains unresolved.

### 4.6 Cross-cutting notes

- Next.js / RSC / Server Actions: no advisory against `next@15.5.29` appears in any current audit result. The previously reported Next/RSC advisories are absent from the candidate.
- Sharp: `sharp@0.35.5` is installed via Next's optional dependency (lockfile `@img/sharp-*@0.35.5`, libvips 1.3.4) and matches Next 15.5.x's documented ≥0.35.5 workaround class for the October SVG advisory; **no sharp advisory appears in the current audits**. Local OS/CPU/libc ≠ Vercel's image pipeline; the installed instance cannot be verified against Vercel runtime from lockfile data alone — flagged for Phase 04/Beta verification.
- PostCSS build-context assumptions (`from` unset? map option? Turbopack vs webpack for `next build`?) remain **unverified**; they are noted, not assumed safe. The mitigation for all four advisories is the absence of untrusted CSS input, which _was_ verified.

## 7. Release gate

**NEEDS OWNER SECURITY DECISION.** Phase 03 investigation is complete and every current production advisory has an evidence-backed, per-advisory disposition (§4). The four postcss findings (R1) ship in the candidate as unresolved vulnerabilities with low demonstrated exposure under documented assumptions — they are **not** accepted, not overridden, and not cleared. Accepting them for v1.1.1, or authorizing further remediation, is a release-owner call — not an agent call. Investigating is not the same as clearing the release.

Phase 03 status: **COMPLETE (pending owner sign-off on R1)**. Audit retrieval succeeded and was reproduced at review; all current production advisories dispositioned; fixes proven by re-audit and frozen install.
